penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Self-hosted Postfix/Mailman3 deliverability tuning is highly environment-specific; meaningful help requires per-customer server access and configuration work, not automated delivery.

rationale: The buyer segment — sysadmins running self-hosted Mailman3/Postfix for organizations — is small, fragmented, and unlikely to pay for a SaaS deliverability tool when the underlying infrastructure is deliberately self-hosted to avoid vendor lock-in. Willingness to pay is weak (score 4): the self-hosting choice itself signals a preference against managed services. The solution is inherently per-customer configuration work requiring server access, which fails the autonomy requirement. Single-signal evidence (one ServeFault post) gives low confidence. Total 2.8 falls well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended for this factory. Self-hosted email deliverability is a niche that by definition attracts operators who prefer to manage their own infrastructure and avoid paid tools. Each customer engagement would require hands-on server-level configuration. A solo non-technical operator cannot deliver this autonomously, and the addressable market of organizations running Mailman3 at scale is small enough that even full capture would not yield meaningful revenue. Pass.
notes: Single weak signal (signal_strength 2). Fails operational_autonomy build gate (score 5, minimum 7). Fails buyer_clarity build gate (score 4, minimum 6). Fails willingness_to_pay build gate (score 4, minimum 5). Total 2.8 well below min_total_to_validate.
